title: Implicit Feedback & Negative Sampling
interviewAnswer: Clicks, views and purchases indicate exposure and preference imperfectly. Unobserved items are not necessarily negatives, so training often samples negatives or uses exposure-aware weighting.
why: Implicit Feedback & Negative Sampling appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Clicks, views and purchases indicate exposure and preference imperfectly. Unobserved items are not necessarily negatives, so training often samples negatives or uses exposure-aware weighting. Different actions imply different strengths. Sampling distribution changes learning. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Treat purchases as strong positives, clicks as weaker signals and sample from exposed-but-not-clicked items more carefully than random catalog negatives.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Implicit Feedback & Negative Sampling make?
How would you validate or debug Implicit Feedback & Negative Sampling in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
